intended_object: The canonical isomorphism between the homology of a short complex S (when it has homology) and the object H of any left homology data h for S. Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation: The definition composes two canonical isomorphisms. The first is the inverse of `S.leftHomologyIso : S.leftHomology ≅ S.homology`. The second is `h.leftHomologyIso : S.leftHomology ≅ h.H`, which compares the chosen left homology with the object H of the given left homology data. The result is the expected canonical isomorphism `S.homology ≅ h.H`, matching the docstring. The setting is the general one for this construction: an arbitrary category with zero morphisms, with the `HasHomology` assumption needed for `S.homology` to exist. I did not search Mathlib for a separate definition of the same isomorphism, since this declaration is itself in Mathlib (`Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/ShortComplex/Homology.lean`); hence the empty counterpart field.
